headline: Bullpen Meltdown At Fenway Ruins Payton Tolle Masterclass Against Twins
morning_brew: We had a four-run lead early after a huge first inning, and it looked like the local nine were going to keep the good times rolling. Payton Tolle was absolutely dealing on the mound, racking up nine strikeouts over six strong innings and looking like a real cornerstone for this rotation. But then the seventh inning happened, and the wheels completely came off the wagon. Justin Slaten got absolutely hammered, giving up four runs on four hits, including a pair of two-run homers to Byron Buxton and Austin Martin. Just like that, our three-game winning streak went right down the drain in an eight to six loss.

I'll tell you exactly what's wrong with this bullpen, we cannot protect a lead to save our lives when the pressure gets turned up. Slaten has been reliable for parts of this year, but leaving him out there to get chewed up by the Minnesota bats was painful to watch. The offense did what they could, with Nick Sogard and Wilyer Abreu both picking up two hits apiece, but you cannot commit two errors and expect to beat a decent ballclub. This loss drops us to twenty-two and twenty-eight, and it feels like we are right back to square one.

At least there is some good news coming out of the basketball offseason with Derrick White making the NBA All-Defensive First Team. It is a well-deserved honor for a guy who gives maximum effort every single night on the parquet and never complains about his role. While the sting of that first-round exit to Philadelphia still lingers, seeing White get recognized alongside guys like Victor Wembanyama is a nice reminder of the talent we have. Let us hope the front office uses this quiet period to build a better supporting cast around him and Jayson Tatum.

news_digest.dans_take: Derrick White getting a first-team nod is a great tribute to the hardest-working guard in the league.
